OpenTelemetry logs and traces

Source: vignettes/opentelemetry.Rmd
opentelemetry.Rmd

Overview

OpenTelemetry sends diagnostic information to a monitoring service. Logs record events such as failed logins, while traces time the operations involved so you can locate a slow token exchange or other provider request. A span is one timed operation within a trace.

For an R callback that receives events directly, see Audit logging.

shinyOAuth uses the otel package to create records. An exporter sends those records to the console or your monitoring service; install otelsdk to provide one.

Exporter configuration

Start with console output to check the setup locally. Run this in a fresh R session, before loading shinyOAuth or starting the app:

# install.packages("otelsdk")
Sys.setenv(
  OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER = "console",
  OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER = "console",
  OTEL_LOG_LEVEL = "debug"
)
library(shinyOAuth)

Sign in with the example app and look for login and callback records in the console. If nothing appears, check that logging and tracing are enabled and restart R after changing the exporter.

Once that works, follow the otelsdk exporter setup and your monitoring service’s endpoint and credential instructions.

Traces and event correlation

Filter by instrumentation scope io.github.lukakoning.shinyOAuth. Start with shinyOAuth.login.request and shinyOAuth.callback, then inspect token exchange or profile-fetch spans to find the slow or failing operation.

The shinyoauth.trace_id attribute connects logs and spans from the same package operation. It is separate from OpenTelemetry’s own trace and span IDs. Logs describe the same events as the audit hook.

Logging and tracing options

shinyOAuth enables logging and tracing by default; an exporter collects the records. If your monitoring service only needs one, disable the other:

options(
  shinyOAuth.otel_logging_enabled = FALSE,
  shinyOAuth.otel_tracing_enabled = FALSE
)

Protecting diagnostic data

By default, shinyOAuth omits raw tokens, detailed error messages, URL paths, query strings, and scope or claim names. Counts remain available. shinyOAuth.telemetry_path_scrubber adds approved route labels, while shinyOAuth.expose_error_body separately controls diagnostic text.

Authorization metadata privacy

Permission names can help explain a failed authorization. This option adds those names to the exported records:

options(shinyOAuth.otel_include_authorization_details = TRUE)

The added names can identify privileges, tenants or data categories. This option is independent of detailed error-message exposure.

Asynchronous workers

shinyOAuth passes exporter environment variables and trace context to its background workers. It does not replay R setup code, so exporters configured through R require their initialization in each worker.

Advanced diagnostic fields

Error attributes and redaction

Successful operations normally have status ok, and failures have status error. For revocation and introspection, missing tokens or unsupported endpoints leave status unset. An inactive token is a successful introspection response (oauth.active = FALSE). Thrown errors also record an exception event with the error class.

Log messages default to the event type. shinyOAuth.expose_error_body can add sanitized diagnostic text during debugging. That text can still contain private provider data. URLs omit paths unless an approved path scrubber supplies a route label. Tokens, codes and raw login state stay out of ordinary span attributes.

These protections cover records emitted through shinyOAuth. Direct SDK calls and requests sent with httr2::req_perform() follow their own telemetry settings. perform_resource_req() applies shinyOAuth’s request handling.

Span catalog

HTTP spans time network calls; worker spans identify background processing. Attributes appear only when relevant and available. Useful fields include oauth.phase, server.address and http.response.status_code, alongside provider and session digests.

Name What it tells you
shinyOAuth.module.init Authentication module startup.
shinyOAuth.login.request Preparing the authorization request and pending login state.
shinyOAuth.login.par Preparing and validating a pushed authorization request.
shinyOAuth.login.par.http The HTTP request to the PAR endpoint.
shinyOAuth.callback Processing the returning login response.
shinyOAuth.form_post Validating a POST callback before the Shiny session receives it.
shinyOAuth.form_post.bridge Consuming the one-time POST callback handle.
shinyOAuth.callback.validate Callback checks; oauth.phase identifies the check.
shinyOAuth.callback.worker Callback processing in an asynchronous worker.
shinyOAuth.token.exchange Exchanging an authorization code for tokens.
shinyOAuth.token.exchange.http The HTTP token request for code exchange or refresh.
shinyOAuth.token.verify Token type, scope and identity checks after a token response.
shinyOAuth.userinfo Fetching, parsing and validating the user profile.
shinyOAuth.userinfo.http The HTTP request to the profile endpoint.
shinyOAuth.refresh Refreshing tokens, including work dispatched to a worker.
shinyOAuth.refresh.worker The worker-side part of an asynchronous refresh.
shinyOAuth.logout Local logout and the start of token cleanup.
shinyOAuth.session.end.revoke Token cleanup requested when a Shiny session ends.
shinyOAuth.token.revoke A token-revocation operation.
shinyOAuth.token.revoke.http The HTTP request to the revocation endpoint.
shinyOAuth.token.revoke.worker The worker-side part of asynchronous revocation.
shinyOAuth.token.introspect A token-activity check.
shinyOAuth.token.introspect.http The HTTP request to the introspection endpoint.
shinyOAuth.token.introspect.worker The worker-side part of asynchronous introspection.
